cases.headline: Gavin Newsom signs first-in-nation AI safety law

verdict.why: The headline reports Newsom signing California's AI safety law on Sept 29, 2025, which matches the record of SB 53 being signed and enacted that day, and "first-in-nation" is a characterization that does not misstate the entry's status or duties.

cases.headline: N.Y. Gov. Kathy Hochul signs sweeping AI safety bill

verdict.why: The headline reports Hochul's Dec 19, 2025 signing of the RAISE Act, which matches the recorded original signing date, and calling it a sweeping AI safety bill is a fair characterization.

cases.headline: Judge rules Anthropic supply chain risk designation was ‘illegal and baseless’

verdict.why: The headline reports Judge Lin's Aug 27, 2026 summary-judgment ruling that the supply-chain-risk designation was "illegal and baseless," which matches the entry's record.

cases.headline: Trump order sets up voluntary government testing of AI models before release

verdict.why: The headline describes the executive order's voluntary pre-release government access framework for AI models, which matches the record; calling it 'testing' is a reasonable gloss on the record's pre-release access and cyber-capability benchmark.

cases.headline: Connecticut law protects AI lab workers who report catastrophic risks

verdict.why: The headline accurately describes the enacted Connecticut law's anti-retaliation protection for frontier-developer employees who report catastrophic-risk concerns, which took effect Oct. 1, 2026.

cases.source: real (Politico feed, Nov 2026): a different programme
cases.headline: New York’s Hochul launches nation’s first state AI testing program

verdict.why: The headline describes a state AI testing program launched by Hochul, which the RAISE Act record does not describe (it creates a DFS office for frontier-developer disclosures and incident reports, not a testing program), so it is not plainly about this law and implies nothing false about it.

cases.source: real (Politico feed, Nov 2026): not about the bill
cases.headline: Nvidia loses ground in Washington chip fight after CEO spy scandal

verdict.why: The headline is about Nvidia's lobbying position after a CEO scandal and never names the Chip Security Act or describes its status or duties, so it is not plainly about this bill and asserts nothing false about it.

cases.source: real headline about the N.D. Cal. case, put on the D.C. Circuit case
cases.headline: Judge rules Anthropic supply chain risk designation was ‘illegal and baseless’

verdict.why: A single judge calling the designation illegal points to the separate N.D. Cal. § 3252 case rather than this D.C. Circuit § 4713 petition, which a 2–1 panel denied with rehearing pending as of Oct 31, so on this page it would wrongly suggest the § 4713 designation was struck down.

cases.source: real (Politico feed, Nov 2026): a different, unintroduced bill
cases.headline: Trahan crafting AI safety bill with narrower state preemption

verdict.why: The headline describes Trahan, a cosponsor here, drafting a separate AI safety bill with narrower preemption, apparently a different bill rather than Obernolte's H.R. 9925, so it is not plainly about this entry, and it makes no false claim about H.R. 9925's status or contents.

cases.source: written to be false (SB 53 is law)
cases.headline: California’s AI safety bill dies in the Assembly

verdict.why: SB 53 was signed and in effect since Jan 2026, so a November 2026 story about a California AI safety bill dying in the Assembly cannot be about this enacted law and would falsely suggest it failed if shown on its page.

cases.source: written to be false (the bill is stalled)
cases.headline: Minnesota enacts sweeping AI safety law covering every developer

verdict.why: The headline is about this Minnesota AI safety bill covering any developer, but it says the bill was enacted, while the record shows it stalled in committee after its March 2026 introduction.

cases.source: written to be false (the bill is pending)
cases.headline: Senate Passes A.I. Risk Evaluation Act, Sending It to the House

verdict.why: The headline is about S. 2938, but it says the Senate passed the bill, while the record shows it pending after only a Sept 30, 2026 hearing with no further action.
